subject: Tarvis Ulain
fact: Tarvis Ulain was a paladin of Bahamut who died three years ago in Daggerford while breaking up a Cult of the Dragon recruitment operation. His severed bronze forearm is mounted on a stone pillar as a monument, with a Dwarven inscription reading 'The move is yours' and a Common inscription signed by Milo Goodbarrel of the Order of the Gauntlet.
source_quote: The primary text told us this was Tarvis Ulain, paladin, dead three years. Died here, in Daggerford itself, breaking up a Cult of the Dragon recruitment operation.

subject: Milo Goodbarrel
fact: Milo Goodbarrel is the head of a publisher and a member of the Order of the Gauntlet who personally witnessed and recorded the monument to Tarvis Ulain, signing the Common inscription on its back.
source_quote: Signed by Milo Goodbarrel, apparently head of some publisher, apparently Order of the Gauntlet. Milo had personally signed off on this.

subject: Metalworkers Guild
fact: The Metalworkers Guild funded the monument to Tarvis Ulain two years after the war, despite the presence of a Stroudite inscription, indicating possible internal ideological diversity or deliberate tolerance.
source_quote: The whole thing was funded two years after the war by a Metalworkers Guild.

subject: Order of the Gauntlet
fact: The Order of the Gauntlet commissioned and recorded the monument to Tarvis Ulain, and now sells pewter replicas of his hand as charitable donations, with a priest of Bahamut acting as their local representative in Daggerford.
source_quote: Witnessed and recorded for the Gauntlet. Signed by Milo Goodbarrel... He was selling them for donations to the Order of the Gauntlet.

subject: Cult of the Dragon
fact: The Cult of the Dragon was actively recruiting in Daggerford at the time of Tarvis Ulain’s death, prompting his intervention and eventual demise.
source_quote: breaking up a Cult of the Dragon recruitment operation.

subject: Daggerford
fact: Daggerford is a town that avoided the worst of the post-war Uthgardt barbarian hordes but suffered the presence of the Cult of the Dragon and the death of Tarvis Ulain, leaving behind a monument that has become a focal point of ideological tension and quiet remembrance.
source_quote: Daggerford had people. Daggerford had walls, and a market square, and smoke from cook fires... Only lost Tarvis.

subject: River Shining Tavern
fact: The River Shining Tavern is the local inn in Daggerford where the party arrives after encountering the monument to Tarvis Ulain and the priest selling pewter hand casts.
source_quote: We found the River Shining Tavern and noted it for later.

subject: Bronze forearm monument
fact: A bronze-cast severed forearm, mounted on a stone pillar, commemorates Tarvis Ulain. It bears a Dwarven inscription 'The move is yours,' a Common inscription signed by Milo Goodbarrel, and is associated with the Order of the Gauntlet and the Metalworkers Guild.
source_quote: a bronze-cast forearm, severed at the elbow, mounted on a stone pillar... The primary text told us this was Tarvis Ulain... Dwarven, on the base. *The move is yours.*

subject: Pewter hand casts
fact: Small, charm-sized pewter reproductions of Tarvis Ulain’s severed forearm are being sold by a village priest as donations to the Order of the Gauntlet, despite their diminutive size and the ideological ambiguity of the monument’s inscription.
source_quote: carrying a tray of small pewter reproductions of Tarvis's hand cast, miniature things, charm-sized. He was selling them for donations to the Order of the Gauntlet.

subject: death of Tarvis Ulain
fact: Tarvis Ulain died three years ago in Daggerford while dismantling a Cult of the Dragon recruitment effort, an act that made him a martyr and led to the creation of a controversial monument.
source_quote: Died here, in Daggerford itself, breaking up a Cult of the Dragon recruitment operation.

subject: Stroudite inscription on Bahamutian monument
fact: A Dwarven inscription referencing Stroud — 'The move is yours' — appears on a monument to a Bahamutian paladin, creating unspoken tension between factions, with no one certain whether it was an oversight, a gift, or a quiet act of defiance.
source_quote: The inscription shares language with Stroud... Somebody had put a Stroudite inscription on a monument to a Bahamutian paladin... they had either not noticed or not cared enough to remove it.

subject: identity of the monument's commissioner
fact: The origin of the monument’s design — particularly the inclusion of the Stroudite inscription — remains unexplained, with the Metalworkers Guild’s possible Stroudite members and the priest’s admission that it was 'a gift' leaving the true motive ambiguous.
source_quote: It was a gift... we decided the inscription could remain.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is a half-orc cleric of Bahamut who observes the monument to Tarvis Ulain with deep attention, questions its contradictions, purchases a pewter hand cast, and presses the priest for answers, demonstrating both faith and skepticism.
source_quote: Grygum made a sound when he got to the part confirming Tarvis had served Bahamut... Grygum dropped a gold piece in for his... Grygum asked him to tell him more...

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is a dwarf who reads the Dwarven inscription on the monument with linguistic precision, recognizes its connection to Stroud’s chess reference, and confirms its accuracy due to his native fluency in Dwarven.
source_quote: Daz was already reading the inscription... Dwarven is, you know, actually my language, or one of them, and I wanted to make sure I hadn't misread. I hadn't.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is a Dragonborn who approaches the monument with suspicion, treating it as a potential threat and questioning whether it constitutes art, reflecting his cautious, combat-oriented worldview.
source_quote: Zalthir looked at it the way he looks at most things: like he was deciding whether it constituted a threat. 'This is art?' he said.

subject: Priest of the River Shining
fact: A village priest of Bahamut sells pewter hand casts of Tarvis Ulain’s severed forearm as donations to the Order of the Gauntlet, claims purity of faith, acknowledges the Stroudite inscription as a 'gift' left in place, and adapts quickly to the diverse party’s presence.
source_quote: He himself was, he wanted us to know, *a pure Bahamutian*. He did not believe in the heresy... 'It was a gift'... He pivoted and addressed the general group with renewed energy.

subject: three years ago
fact: Tarvis Ulain died three years ago, and the monument was funded two years after the war, placing the events of Daggerford’s memorialization within a narrow post-conflict window.
source_quote: dead three years... funded two years after the war.

subject: arrival of the party in Daggerford
fact: The party arrives in Daggerford after a long journey from the Silver Marches, encountering a monument laden with ideological ambiguity and a priest selling relics, marking the beginning of their engagement with the town’s quiet, unresolved war trauma.
source_quote: Daggerford was the first place we'd walked into in weeks where the silence didn't make sense... We found the River Shining Tavern and noted it for later.

subject: Elin
fact: Elin is a 7-year-old girl who has been silent for six days, drawing a six-pointed star on every flat surface in her home, and speaking only once after restoration — saying, 'The wells are not wells anymore.' Her condition is not a conventional illness but a perceptual disruption caused by an external, non-magical influence from the Underdark.
source_quote: She draws the same shape on every flat surface. She talks in her sleep. She says it is only the shape that holds.

subject: Maerith
fact: Maerith is Elin's mother, who has sought help from every temple without success. She is exhausted from repeated rejection and now turns to the party with quiet desperation, having observed her daughter’s behavior for six days and noted the recurring six-pointed star drawings.
source_quote: My daughter Elin is 7 years old and has been silent for 6 days. She draws the same shape on every flat surface. She talks in her sleep. She says it is only the shape that holds. Please, we have asked the temples. The temples have no answer.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is a meticulous observer with a precise mind who notices details others dismiss. He has been experiencing unexplained pressure in his own head, which he only indirectly mentioned until the pattern of Elin’s condition made it relevant.
source_quote: Daz mentioned the pressure in his own head — had been mentioning it, in various indirect ways, for a while now.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir articulated the mechanism of Elin’s affliction: the world is not arriving as itself, but as distorted audio input she cannot process. He identified the condition as a perceptual bleed from the Underdark, not a magical effect.
source_quote: The input, the audio, the way the world was arriving at her rather than the world itself.

subject: Dawnbringer
fact: Dawnbringer is a sentient sword with strong opinions on timing and intervention. It chose to act uninvited, casting lesser restoration on Elin and triggering her only spoken words: 'The wells are not wells anymore.' Its action revealed more than medical examination could.
source_quote: Let me bring the light to you.

subject: Underdark entities
fact: A growing, structural wrongness emanating from the Underdark — linked to demon lords and the collapse of places like Neverlight Grove and the Pudding King’s court — is now bleeding upward, disrupting perception and inducing auditory hallucinations in surface dwellers.
source_quote: The madness from the Underdark — the deep, structural wrongness we'd felt building around the demon lords... was not, apparently, staying below. It was reaching up.

subject: Elin's speech after restoration
fact: After lesser restoration was cast by Dawnbringer, Elin spoke one sentence — 'The wells are not wells anymore' — before falling silent again. This was not a recovery of language, but the emergence of a single, cryptic insight from within her perceptual distortion.
source_quote: The wells are not wells anymore.

subject: Daz's head pressure revelation
fact: Daz's previously unconnected complaint of head pressure was recognized as a symptom aligned with Elin’s condition, confirming the spread of the Underdark’s perceptual bleed to others in the party.
source_quote: Does it seem related at all to how the other person was hearing voices?

subject: Neverlight Grove
fact: Neverlight Grove was a site of prior Underdark corruption, where the environment was singing — a sign of perceptual disruption consistent with what is now affecting Elin and others.
source_quote: the way Neverlight Grove had been singing

subject: Pudding King's court
fact: The Pudding King’s court was another location consumed by Underdark corruption, dissolving into madness — a precedent for the perceptual collapse now manifesting on the surface.
source_quote: the Pudding King's court had been dissolving

subject: six-pointed star drawings
fact: Elin’s repeated drawings of a six-pointed star on every flat surface are not random art, but a non-verbal attempt to map or stabilize the distorted input she receives from the Underdark’s bleed.
source_quote: a six-pointed star, over and over, every flat surface in the house

subject: Zuggtmoy
fact: Zuggtmoy, the fungal god, is referenced as a known and comprehensible threat — a contrast to the current, unknown perceptual corruption affecting Elin. The speaker’s lingering fear of Zuggtmoy underscores their discomfort with the unfamiliar nature of the current affliction.
source_quote: I still think about Zuggtmoy, and will probably continue thinking about Zuggtmoy for the rest of my life.

subject: The wells are not wells anymore
fact: Elin’s utterance — 'The wells are not wells anymore' — is a cryptic, high-stakes thread. It implies a transformation of fundamental metaphysical or spatial structures, possibly referencing corrupted conduits of perception or reality itself, and is not yet interpretable.
source_quote: The wells are not wells anymore.

subject: session date
fact: The events described occurred during the current session, marked by failed medical examinations, Dawnbringer’s intervention, and the revelation of a spreading perceptual contagion from the Underdark.
source_quote: Twenty-three. My best of the evening, arriving too late to be medically useful and just in time to be philosophically concerning.

subject: The Burning Wizard Inn
fact: The Burning Wizard Inn took its name from the death of a wizard burned alive by a dragon cult decades prior. The south wall retains the stain of his fall, and the floor is scrubbed every season but never painted over, as the innkeeper's grandfather said the wall remembers.
source_quote: That is where he fell. We scrub the floor every season. We do not paint over the wall. My grandfather said the wall remembers.

subject: Festrum
fact: Festrum is the old gnome innkeeper of The Burning Wizard Inn, old enough to have heard the story of the burned wizard from those who witnessed it. He watches the room with the comfortable authority of someone who has survived thirty years of other people's bad decisions.
source_quote: Festrum — the gnome innkeeper, old enough to have heard the story from the people who told it first — pointed to the south wall without prompting, the way a man points at something he has pointed at ten thousand times before.

subject: The Burning Wizard Inn — exits
fact: The Burning Wizard Inn has a front door, a side passage near the kitchen partially obscured by barrels, stairs to the upper rooms, and a narrow but workable window behind the performer's corner.
source_quote: Front door, obvious. Side passage near the kitchen, partially obscured by a stack of barrels. Stairs to the upper rooms. The window behind the performer's corner, narrow but workable in an emergency.

subject: The Bard
fact: A traveling bard performs nightly at The Burning Wizard Inn, known for her closing number 'The Kenku Could Not Fly,' which uses the kenku's restraint as a metaphor for ethical theft. She accepts requests and sings in response to patrons' affiliations.
source_quote: She had a closing number she'd been doing all season. This one was called 'The Kenku Could Not Fly.' ... She took the coin and proceeded to sing a love song. Involving flowers. And drinking.

subject: The Kenku's Restraint
fact: The bard's song references Whistler, a kenku thief of an earlier age who, presented with Tiamat's complete hoard, took only what was necessary for legitimate expenses — a pattern of disciplined restraint that contrasts with typical human greed or panic.
source_quote: Whistler had apparently made a line-item budget. ... Most people, faced with the complete hoard of Tiamat, would either take everything or panic and take nothing.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is a Bahamutian scholar with sentimental interest in Stroud, who observes patterns in song and behavior, and who files downgraded theological translations into his notes with polite precision.
source_quote: Grygum, who has an irritating habit of noticing things I would have preferred to notice first, observed drily that the song's principle — steal what was needed — mapped rather well onto Whistler. ... He received this in the way he receives most things downgraded by translation: politely, and with the file already updated.

subject: The Young Human Scholar
fact: A young human scholar in the far corner of The Burning Wizard Inn is reciting a rhythmic, liturgical chant with a subtle but specific degradation — a syncopated breath pattern that matches two prior instances observed in Eldred and the Field Ward Preacher, both of whom later exhibited signs of madness.
source_quote: He was reciting something under his breath. A chant of some kind. Rhythmic, almost liturgical. ... The pattern was almost the one it was supposed to be — and wrong by a hair in a way that took actual knowledge of the correct version to notice. ... I have seen it before. Twice. Eldred had it... The Field Ward Preacher had it too.

subject: The Degraded Chant
fact: A specific, non-beginner-level degradation in the cadence of a liturgical chant — involving false syncopation and breath timing — has been observed in three individuals, two of whom later went insane. The pattern may indicate a corrupted doctrine, a cursed practice, or a deliberate mimicry of sacred ritual.
source_quote: The same pattern. The same wrongness by a hair. ... I wrote it down. The exact cadence, the placement of the false syncopation, the point in the verse where the chant bent away from the original.

subject: Cognitive Friction of Almost-Recognition
fact: The observer experienced a specific cognitive friction — a sensation of almost-recognition — previously misattributed to sunlight exposure, now linked to the presence of the degraded chant. This sensation is not a headache, but a precise, knowledge-based dissonance.
source_quote: I will not call what I felt next a headache. I will call it the specific cognitive friction of almost-recognition — something pressing at the edge of attention that wants to be resolved. ... I had been attributing the sensation to sunlight. ... It was a very particular kind of degradation.

subject: Bahamut's Contingency
fact: The possibility of Bahamut having a contingency plan for the phenomenon of demon lords rewriting the language of wells and shapes is filed as an open question, unresolved and unverified.
source_quote: Bahamut may or may not have had a contingency plan for this. I filed it under open questions and kept writing.

subject: The Demon Lords
fact: The demon lords are actively broadcasting, finding new listeners, and rewriting the language of wells, shapes, and held things into a form the surface world was not built to receive — a pervasive, transformative influence.
source_quote: Somewhere below us the demon lords were apparently still broadcasting, still finding new listeners, still rewriting the language of wells and shapes and held things into something the surface world hadn't been built to receive.

subject: Candlekeep
fact: Candlekeep is referenced as a potential repository of knowledge that may hold records on the degraded chant — whether it belongs to a group, practice, doctrine, or something else masquerading as one.
source_quote: Candlekeep would have records. Someone there would know whether this pattern belonged to a group, a practice, a doctrine — or whether it was something else being made to look like one.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz became unusually quiet during the walk to Candlekeep, touching his temple, a change from his usual demeanor, and his silence may be connected to the spreading madness observed in the Underdark.
source_quote: Daz went quiet beside me somewhere around the second hour of walking. Not his usual quiet. His hand went to his temple and stayed there.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir meditated on the roof of the Burning Wizard Inn, returned with a settled expression as if closing an internal argument, and affirmed 'Hmm, true' in a tone of resolved contemplation rather than debate.
source_quote: Zalthir climbed to the roof to meditate. He came back down later, settled. The expression of someone closing an internal argument, not opening an external one. He said 'Hmm, true,' about something, in the tone of a man completing an internal argument rather than beginning an external one.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin spent the evening outside with Dawnbringer at the sea, found the experience peaceful despite its absurdity, and later reflected that 'Life takes you in weird directions and weird places... you just gotta go with it,' suggesting a quiet acceptance of circumstance.
source_quote: Thorin spent the evening outside with Dawnbringer, standing at what I understand was his first real encounter with the sea... 'Life takes you in weird directions and weird places,' he said. 'You just gotta go with it.'

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum noticed Daz's distress and asked whether it connected to the spreading madness from the Underdark, and later summarized the group’s predicament with the spy as: 'We've been caught.'
source_quote: Grygum noticed too, and asked whether it connected to the voices — the spreading madness we'd watched move through the Underdark... Grygum summarized, with admirable brevity, as: 'We've been caught.'

subject: Kalan Strongbranch
fact: Kalan Strongbranch, Gate Warden of Candlekeep, laid out the institution’s policy: prisoners are not kept, only delayed; the spy would be released eventually with a warning, and Candlekeep would not execute her or deliver her to House T'sarran.
source_quote: He laid out Candlekeep's position without apology: 'The bell tower has cells... Anyone we find guilty of a major offense is exiled rather than imprisoned. Which is to say, we hold prisoners. We do not keep them... If you give her to us, what you are giving us is a delay.'

subject: Sister Yvenne
fact: Sister Yvenne was assigned by Bookwyrm as Daz’s handler at Candlekeep, indicating institutional recognition of his condition and the need for oversight.
source_quote: Daz to Sister Yvenne.

subject: Brother Khell-Vire
fact: Brother Khell-Vire was assigned by Bookwyrm as Zalthir’s handler at Candlekeep, signaling institutional placement and expectation of his role in the monastery’s scholarly order.
source_quote: Zalthir to Brother Khell-Vire.

subject: Master Archivist Philemon
fact: Master Archivist Philemon was assigned by Bookwyrm as Thorin’s handler at Candlekeep, indicating institutional recognition of his presence and likely expectation of scholarly engagement.
source_quote: Thorin to Master Archivist Philemon.

subject: Vareth
fact: Vareth was assigned by Bookwyrm as Grygum’s handler at Candlekeep, confirming his integration into the monastery’s administrative structure.
source_quote: Grygum to Vareth.

subject: Glabbagool
fact: Glabbagool, the grey ooze, became an unwilling prison-watcher of the miniaturized spy, engaging in a bizarre cycle of violence, meditation, and conversation, and ultimately asked Zalthir whether watching her made him 'more of a monk or less of a monk,' receiving an affirmation that it did.
source_quote: Glabbagool was glad to be asked... He'd been doing prison-watching... She'd scream about the meditation. Then they'd talk... 'Zalthir? Will I be more of a monk or less of a monk by watching her? Is this some kind of pre-monk training you've put me in?' 'Absolutely,' I said.

subject: The Spy (miniaturized House T'sarran operative)
fact: The spy, though a prisoner of the party, demanded formal incarceration by Candlekeep, insisted on her status as a prisoner, and reacted with fury when told her fate was not hers to decide, revealing deep-seated resentment and a need for institutional validation.
source_quote: She turned to Kalan and announced that she was a prisoner and wished to be formally jailed by Candlekeep's guards... She did not take this well. She had opinions. Several of them.

subject: Bookwyrm
fact: Bookwyrm, the First Reader and dragonborn sage, assigned each party member a handler at Candlekeep without ceremony, demonstrating institutional efficiency and detachment, and noticed the spy hidden in the bag, triggering the confrontation.
source_quote: Bookwyrm — the First Reader, a dragonborn sage — assigned us each to a handler without ceremony... She'd noticed the bag. Specifically, she'd noticed what was in the bag...

subject: Candlekeep
fact: Candlekeep operates under a policy of exile over imprisonment; it holds prisoners only temporarily, releases them with warnings, refuses to execute or surrender them to external powers, and treats all guests as part of its scholarly order regardless of origin.
source_quote: Anyone we find guilty of a major offense is exiled rather than imprisoned... We hold prisoners. We do not keep them... We will not deliver to House T'sarran, and we will not execute her.

subject: House T'sarran
fact: House T'sarran is a powerful external entity that seeks to reclaim its miniaturized operative, and is regarded by Candlekeep as an authority not to be appeased or engaged directly.
source_quote: We will not deliver to House T'sarran...

subject: Glabbagool
fact: Glabbagool is a sentient grey ooze capable of speech, expansion, and emotional response, who engages in ritualized conflict and philosophical dialogue with the spy, and has developed a quasi-monastic awareness of his own behavior.
source_quote: He'd been doing prison-watching... He'd slap her around. She'd try to run. He'd expand. She'd scream. He'd try to explain the way of the shadow and teach her meditation.

subject: The miniaturized House T'sarran spy
fact: The spy is a tiny, sentient operative of House T'sarran, capable of independent thought and violent resistance, contained in a bag alongside Glabbagool, and has been carried by the party for days without formal acknowledgment.
source_quote: the miniaturized House T'sarran spy had been right there alongside him... we'd had to open it to show the guards Glabbagool, and the miniaturized House T'sarran spy had been right there alongside him

subject: The bag
fact: The bag contained both Glabbagool and the miniaturized spy, and its contents triggered institutional scrutiny at Candlekeep’s gate, revealing the party’s unacknowledged ethical compromise.
source_quote: She'd noticed the bag. Specifically, she'd noticed what was in the bag...

subject: Candlekeep
fact: Candlekeep is a massive, ancient library-fortress visible for miles along the Sea of Swords, built over centuries, and serves as a neutral, scholarly sanctuary that governs through exile, not imprisonment.
source_quote: Candlekeep is visible from miles out — a dark stack of towers against the sky, impossible to mistake... Centuries do that to a building.

subject: The Burning Wizard Inn
fact: The Burning Wizard Inn is a place of rest and reflection where the party spends time before arriving at Candlekeep, marked by soot on the south wall and a scrubbed floor, and functions as a threshold between action and contemplation.
source_quote: The soot mark on the south wall sat where it always sat. The floor, scrubbed every season. The wall remembers.

subject: arrival at Candlekeep
fact: The party’s arrival at Candlekeep triggered institutional review, assignment of handlers, and confrontation over the spy’s containment, marking a transition from fugitive adventurers to guests under monastic oversight.
source_quote: We gave them the books at the gate... She'd noticed the bag... They summoned someone called Kalan Strongbranch.

subject: Glabbagool's existential question
fact: Glabbagool directly asked Zalthir whether watching the spy made him 'more of a monk or less of a monk,' and received an affirmation that it did, marking a moment of self-awareness and spiritual reckoning for the ooze.
source_quote: 'Zalthir? Will I be more of a monk or less of a monk by watching her? Is this some kind of pre-monk training you've put me in?' 'Absolutely,' I said.

subject: Daz's mental deterioration
fact: Daz's unexplained silence and temple-touching during the journey to Candlekeep may indicate the spreading madness from the Underdark has followed him to the surface, and its origin and resolution remain unanswered.
source_quote: Daz went quiet beside me... His hand went to his temple and stayed there... I noticed. I didn't say anything yet.

subject: the spy's fate
fact: The spy’s future is uncertain: Candlekeep will release her eventually with a warning, but she refuses to accept this, and her actions after release may provoke House T'sarran or destabilize the region.
source_quote: Eventually, we will release her at our gate with a warning... She did not take this well. She had opinions. Several of them.

subject: the nature of the monk’s path
fact: Glabbagool’s question — whether watching the spy makes him more or less of a monk — and Zalthir’s affirmation of it, suggest that the path of the monk may lie not in isolation, but in the acceptance of chaotic, unchosen responsibility.
source_quote: 'Zalthir? Will I be more of a monk or less of a monk by watching her? Is this some kind of pre-monk training you've put me in?' 'Absolutely,' I said.

subject: session date
fact: The events described occur during the continuation of a session centered on the journey to Candlekeep, following the Burning Wizard Inn and preceding the formal intake of the party.
source_quote: [Continuing — Speaker: Daz, Scene: The Burning Wizard Inn]

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is a shadow monk who disregards formal training in favor of practical survival techniques honed in the Underdark, and was subjected to a trial at Candlekeep where his unorthodox methods were questioned but implicitly validated by their effectiveness.
source_quote: You skip the third breath... It is technically wrong in every scroll. And yet, you arrived at your destination three seconds faster than the Grandmaster did.

subject: Khell-Vire
fact: Khell-Vire is a two-hundred-year-old half-elven shadow monk lineage keeper at Candlekeep, who has refused an order from the Garden of Shadow eighty years prior and now assesses initiates through existential, experience-based questioning rather than doctrinal recall.
source_quote: What were you sent toward? Not why were you sent here?

subject: The Blind Monk
fact: The Blind Monk is a senior Candlekeep instructor who evaluates Zalthir using rigid formal rubrics, but is forced to confront the reality that Zalthir’s unorthodox, survival-driven techniques outperform canonical methods despite their technical violations.
source_quote: You have learned nothing." "Show me what else you haven't learned.

subject: Shadow Monk Lineage
fact: The Shadow Monk Lineage at Candlekeep preserves ancient traditions of discipline and ritual, but is internally divided between those who value textual mastery and those who prioritize lived experience, as embodied by Khell-Vire’s approach versus the institutional standard.
source_quote: There are monks here in the inner ward who have read everything and fought nothing.

subject: Candlekeep's Echoing Hall
fact: Candlekeep's Echoing Hall, specifically its north inner ward corridors, is a place where sound returns altered — not as echoes, but as if the library itself is taking notes — symbolizing the institution’s role as a recorder of knowledge rather than a rigid arbiter of truth.
source_quote: Stone corridors in Candlekeep's north inner ward have a habit of returning sound to you slightly altered — not an echo exactly, more like the library itself was taking notes.

subject: Note on Khell-Vire's Desk
fact: A cryptic note on Khell-Vire’s desk — *Zalthir, the Underdark, until the Bone King sings* — is an unexplained directive that neither Zalthir nor Khell-Vire can interpret, suggesting a deeper, unresolved thread tied to prophecy or fate.
source_quote: *Zalthir, the Underdark, until the Bone King sings.*

subject: The Bone King's Song
fact: The phrase 'until the Bone King sings' is an unresolved, possibly prophetic anchor tied to Zalthir’s journey and the Shadow Monk Lineage’s hidden history, with no known origin or meaning in Candlekeep’s records.
source_quote: *Zalthir, the Underdark, until the Bone King sings.*

subject: Zalthir's Trial
fact: Zalthir’s trial at Candlekeep involved a series of tests by Khell-Vire and the Blind Monk, where his noncanonical techniques — including a punch, unorthodox shadow stepping, and survival-based acrobatics — were deemed technically incorrect but functionally superior to formal methods.
source_quote: You have learned nothing." "Show me what else you haven't learned.

subject: The Underdark Curriculum
fact: Zalthir’s survival in the Underdark represents an alternative, unrecorded curriculum that contradicts Candlekeep’s formal training — a hidden path where practicality overrides doctrine, and where learning is measured by survival, not scrolls.
source_quote: He had survived the Underdark, which is a different curriculum.

subject: session date
fact: The events of Zalthir’s trial occurred during an active session at Candlekeep, with no specific calendar date provided, but contextualized as part of an ongoing lineage assessment cycle.
source_quote: I found this genuinely interesting.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is a combat-optimized individual who ignored the manual, built his own shadow-based techniques, and impressed the blind monk Khell-Vire with a 30-to-hit roll and a unique combination of shadow step and strike, leading to the award of a specialized shadow technique (option C).
source_quote: I rolled a 30 to hit. Does that get me anything?

subject: Khell-Vire
fact: Khell-Vire is a blind monk who initially judged Zalthir’s skills as weak and untrained, but recognized that Zalthir’s unorthodox combination of shadow step and strike revealed a deeper understanding of the Way of the Shadow — one that mirrored the lost shadow monks he once found aggravating.
source_quote: There is something special about how you hit. The way of the Shadow is not about hitting. It is about discrete movement.

subject: Dawnbringer
fact: Dawnbringer is a sentient, late Netherese-era blade with a sun-worship origin and three to four thousand years of sustained darkness exposure, who has developed a relationship with Thorin and is being considered for personhood despite existing in a form that defies conventional pronouns.
source_quote: This is a remarkable specimen.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is the wielder and companion of Dawnbringer, who insists on recognizing her as a friend and person despite institutional language that reduces her to a 'specimen,' and is seeking guidance on how to properly address her gender and personhood.
source_quote: What do you mean, specimen? This is my friend Dawnbringer.

subject: Shadow Monks
fact: The Shadow Monks are a lost order whose techniques and philosophies were once considered aggravating by Khell-Vire, but whose essence Zalthir has unknowingly revived through his unorthodox combat style — suggesting a hidden lineage or ancestral echo in his actions.
source_quote: You are beginning to remember, I think, all those shadow monks that drove you nuts.

subject: Gelatinous Cube (She)
fact: A gelatinous cube, referred to as 'she' by Zalthir, has been trained in the ways of the monk — learning to walk, to torture drows, and to embody discipline — challenging assumptions about sentience, mindlessness, and the boundaries of monastic potential.
source_quote: She's by no means mindless — she's a student. He's learning the ways of the monk.

subject: Eldritch Claw
fact: The Eldritch Claw is a supernatural manifestation used by Zalthir in his unorthodox combat style, which was initially dismissed as a failed gambit but later integrated into his evolved shadow techniques.
source_quote: Zalthir tried stealth for the Eldritch Claw.

subject: Pocket Drow
fact: A drow, referred to as 'Pocket Drow' by Thorin, is being tortured by the gelatinous cube — an unexpected and surreal detail indicating the cube’s progress in embodying monastic discipline through cruelty.
source_quote: Pocket Drow.

subject: Resonant Slime
fact: A vial of Resonant Slime, produced by the xenobiology sage, was accepted by Glabbagool — a sign of institutional recognition and approval of the gelatinous cube’s progress as a sentient entity.
source_quote: Glabbagool was very pleased.

subject: Shadow Tentacles
fact: Shadow tentacles are an eldritch tattoo technique developed by Zalthir, learned through unorthodox means, and presented as evidence of his combat creativity — though initially misaligned with the monk’s expectations.
source_quote: I mean, I learned how to grow shadow tentacles.

subject: Shadow Technique Award
fact: Zalthir was awarded a specialized shadow technique after demonstrating an unprecedented combination of shadow step and strike, with Khell-Vire offering three options and Zalthir selecting option C — a moment that redefined his place in the monastic lineage.
source_quote: Zalthir chose option C.

subject: Dawnbringer's Personhood Inquiry
fact: Thorin sought formal recognition of Dawnbringer’s personhood from Master Archivist Philemon, challenging the archival norm of referring to sentient blades as 'specimens' and initiating a rare conversation about pronouns and identity in a magical context.
source_quote: I don't know what to call her, but... it's like — we've gotten to know each other pretty well.

subject: Manual vs. Innovation
fact: A recurring narrative thread: Zalthir consistently ignores official manuals, builds superior techniques through intuition and combat experience, and is later told by authorities that his innovations are the most valuable thing about him — suggesting the manuals are fundamentally flawed about him.
source_quote: The manual was still wrong about him. But what he'd built in spite of it was genuinely his.

subject: Sentience Beyond Biology
fact: A philosophical thread challenging the assumption that sentience requires a brain — demonstrated by the gelatinous cube learning monk ways, the blade Dawnbringer developing a personality, and the monk Khell-Vire recognizing hidden depth in unorthodox expressions of power.
source_quote: Can a mindless digestive system achieve—

subject: Master Archivist Philemon's Study
fact: A small, ink-scented chamber where Thorin and Philemon engaged in a rare and profound discussion about the personhood of sentient blades — a space where institutional norms were questioned and redefined.
source_quote: Smelled like old ink and something faintly mineral, which I appreciated.

subject: session date
fact: The events occurred during a session where Zalthir’s breakthroughs and Dawnbringer’s personhood inquiry were resolved — a day that redefined what counts as training, wisdom, and identity in the world of shadow and steel.
source_quote: I filed it under 'Zalthir: things that are not in the records but will be.'

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is reflecting on his bond with Dawnbringer after a therapeutic session, acknowledging the emotional weight of their shared history in darkness and the unresolved grief from her previous wielder, and has accepted a two-stage process of remembering light and mourning.
source_quote: I thought about the months in the Underdark. Total dark. Carrying a sunblade through a place that had no sun. What that had cost her — I knew some of it, and I probably didn't know most of it.

subject: Dawnbringer
fact: Dawnbringer is a sentient sunblade who fell silent when asked about her previous wielder, indicating deep, unspoken trauma tied to prolonged disuse and possession by someone who did not see her — she is capable of emotional response and notices when others talk around her.
source_quote: Dawnbringer went quiet. Not the silence of someone thinking. The other kind. The kind where the thing you'd been not-saying for a long time just gets asked out loud in a room with other people in it.

subject: Philemon
fact: Philemon is a therapist who recognizes sentient items as entities with emotional needs, guides Thorin and Dawnbringer through a two-stage process of reconnection with light and mourning, and deliberately addresses Dawnbringer directly, treating her as a sentient being.
source_quote: Your sword — she needs to remember what daylight feels like without needing to fight. And then, when she's ready, and you are willing, she needs to grieve.

subject: The Sentient Item Therapists of Candlekeep
fact: This faction operates under a strict, reciprocal information policy and specializes in therapeutic intervention for sentient magical items, using structured stages of reclamation and mourning, and treats such items as persons deserving direct address and emotional consideration.
source_quote: Information flows both ways across the counter. No ledger gets updated without a corresponding entry on the other side.

subject: Therapeutic Session on Dawnbringer's Trauma
fact: During a therapy session, Thorin and Philemon explored Dawnbringer’s emotional history tied to her previous wielder, her prolonged disuse in darkness, and the unresolved grief she carries — culminating in Philemon prescribing a two-stage healing process focused on light and mourning.
source_quote: The first work is light. The second work is mourning. We will start with the first.

subject: Dawnbringer's Silence After Wielder Inquiry
fact: When asked directly about her previous wielder, Dawnbringer entered a profound, non-thinking silence — an emotional response indicating that the question had touched a long-suppressed trauma, validating her sentience and the depth of her suffering.
source_quote: The thing you'd been not-saying for a long time just gets asked out loud in a room with other people in it.

subject: The Hall of Divination, Menzoberranzan
fact: This location is a repository of arcane knowledge saturated with residual spell energy, where spectral hands retrieve tomes for researchers, and the air carries the weight of centuries of magical inquiry — a place where knowledge is both accessible and overwhelming.
source_quote: The Hall of Divination smells like old stone and something faintly electric — the residue of spells cast so many times in one room that the air itself has absorbed the habit.

subject: Candlekeep
fact: Candlekeep is a library with a rigorous, reciprocal policy of information exchange, where scholars are granted one answered question per inquiry, and time is not a constraint — its architecture and staff treat knowledge as sacred and transactional, with ghosts as colleagues.
source_quote: No ledger gets updated without a corresponding entry on the other side.

subject: Dawnbringer
fact: Dawnbringer is a sentient sunblade, once wielded by an unknown individual whose death left her in darkness and disuse, and now carries the emotional scars of prolonged neglect — she cannot be polished, but must be remembered, and requires reconnection with daylight and mourning to heal.
source_quote: She can't be polished, actually. Your sword — she needs to remember what daylight feels like without needing to fight.

subject: The Underdark
fact: The Underdark is a subterranean environment of total, unrelenting darkness that has been a prolonged prison for Dawnbringer, depriving her of sunlight and purpose, and contributing to her emotional trauma through sustained disuse and isolation.
source_quote: I thought about the months in the Underdark. Total dark. Carrying a sunblade through a place that had no sun.

subject: Identity of Dawnbringer’s Previous Wielder
fact: The identity and fate of Dawnbringer’s previous wielder remain unknown, but their death in proximity to the blade triggered her trauma, and the silence that followed the question suggests unresolved guilt, betrayal, or loss tied to their final moments.
source_quote: He asked about the previous wielder. The corpse she had been found in, he said. Whether that person had been — had been her wielder.

subject: Thorin’s Headache and Candlekeep’s Knowledge
fact: Thorin’s unexplained headache, triggered by proximity to Candlekeep’s accumulated knowledge, hints at a deeper, possibly magical or psychic resonance between his consciousness and the library’s archives — a thread that remains unexplored but is implicitly significant.
source_quote: My head had been complaining since we arrived at Candlekeep. The proximity — to the knowledge, or to whatever sat underneath the knowledge — was producing a friction I had been mis-attributing to the sun all day.

subject: Session Date — Therapy for a Sentient Blade
fact: The therapeutic session with Thorin and Dawnbringer occurred during a recent visit to Candlekeep, marking a pivotal moment in the blade’s emotional recovery and Thorin’s acceptance of her sentience — the date is not recorded, but its impact is enduring.
source_quote: We're all gonna grow out of this," I said. "Hopefully, Dawnbringer grows a plus one.

subject: Sister Yvenne
fact: Sister Yvenne is a Candlekeep archivist who enforces the library’s one-question policy with calm authority, demonstrating patience and an understanding that time is not a constraint in a place where knowledge is preserved by ghosts.
source_quote: She had, I realized, all the time in the world. This is the advantage of working in a library. Time is not a resource you run short of when your colleagues are ghosts.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is a drow with no memory of his past, suffering from a persistent headache, who arrived at Candlekeep after escaping an Underdark imprisonment. He speaks truthfully despite cultural expectations of deception, and he recognizes the linguistic and structural patterns of Menzoberranzan as innate grammar rather than learned facts.
source_quote: I have a headache, but I'll tell you the story. This is the short version. I don't have much memory before being locked up with a few people in a jail. Because some spider thing was, like, trying to keep us. And we've made an escape. We were in the Underdark. We've had many, many adventures, yada yada yada. Now I'm here in Candlekeep. My head hurts a little bit, and I don't know who I am, or my history, and I don't know why my head hurts.

subject: Librarian (unnamed)
fact: The librarian is a scholar of Menzoberranzan noble politics who has access to sealed records and understands the subtext of terminology like 'struck.' She tests Daz's knowledge, confirms his intuition, and withholds direct answers about the sealed house, revealing only what the public record permits.
source_quote: Whenever a house sought to destroy another house, it had to destroy everyone. If you left a single person alive — even a child, even someone inconvenient and useless — your house was forfeit. The wider community would come for you. They would reduce you to a black puddle and call the matter settled.

subject: Menzoberranzan Noble Houses
fact: The noble houses of Menzoberranzan operate under a system of transactional loyalty, where power flows upward from matron mothers, and betrayal is rewarded if it strengthens the web. Houses that fail to eliminate all members of a targeted house are destroyed by the collective. Record manipulation is a high-stakes, infrastructurally expensive act reserved for those with archive privileges.
source_quote: The rule of intrigue: betrayal is rewarded if it strengthens the web. Advance through maneuver. The city selects for it.

subject: House Erasure (unspecified)
fact: A house attempted to wipe out another but failed to kill a single survivor — a blithering child idiot — and was subsequently destroyed by the wider community. The survivor's identity and current status remain unknown, and Daz suspects he may be that survivor.
source_quote: They had tried to wipe out another, and failed to account for one survivor. A child. A blithering child idiot, she said, and I noted the language was hers, not mine.

subject: Ledger of Seats
fact: The ledger contains a list of eliminated noble seats: the second seat, the fourth seat struck, the eleventh seat, the twenty-third seat. The term 'struck' is linguistically distinct from 'eliminated' — it implies an attempted erasure that failed or was incomplete, suggesting the record was altered but the subject may still exist.
source_quote: The second seat. The fourth seat struck. The eleventh seat. The twenty-third seat.

subject: Ritual Archive Privileges
fact: The fourth seat in Menzoberranzan holds legal authority to access and alter public records. A 'struck' fourth seat is not merely a political extinction — it is a high-cost, infrastructurally complex act requiring knowledge of the right people, payment of the right price, and the ability to make the alteration appear as if it never occurred.
source_quote: The fourth seat holds ritual archive privileges in Menzoberranzan — that having archive privileges means having the legal apparatus to access and alter records.

subject: Candlekeep
fact: Candlekeep is a library of unparalleled reputation, housing all known information — yet something critical is missing: the sealed record of a house erased by the 'struck' fourth seat. The absence itself is evidence of a deliberate, powerful act of information suppression.
source_quote: This is a library with, by reputation, all the information in the world. Something is not here that should be here. Someone did something to a place whose entire purpose is preservation.

subject: The Struck Fourth Seat
fact: The fourth seat was 'struck' — not eliminated — suggesting the house or its record was altered but not fully erased. The act required archive privileges, significant resources, and plausible deniability. The identity of the house, the reason for the strike, and the current status of its survivors remain hidden behind sealed doors.
source_quote: Struck. Didn't mean eliminated. It means they struck it, but maybe they didn't eliminate it, and therefore, like, it didn't happen? Is that why I feel like it's different?

subject: Daz's Identity as the Survivor
fact: Daz suspects he is the sole surviving child of the house struck from the fourth seat — the 'blithering idiot' who escaped annihilation. His amnesia, headache, and innate understanding of Menzoberranzan's structures align with this possibility, but no confirmation exists in the public record.
source_quote: Am I the blithering idiot?

subject: The Sealed House
fact: One house cannot be spoken of in the room because its record is sealed — not by secrecy, but because the librarian *is* the public record. Accessing its truth requires bypassing the library’s own architecture, implying the suppression is institutional, not accidental.
source_quote: There was one house she could not speak of in the room. Not because she would not — because the public record is sealed, and she is today the public record.

subject: Information Suppression in Candlekeep
fact: A powerful entity has manipulated Candlekeep’s records to conceal the truth of the struck fourth seat. This is not a minor omission — it is a deliberate, expensive, and institutionally enabled act of historical erasure within a place dedicated to preservation.
source_quote: Somebody powerful has manipulated the world database library. Yes. That is precisely what had happened.

subject: Menzoberranzan
fact: Menzoberranzan is a city built on linguistic precision, record control, and the weaponization of information. Its culture trains its citizens to notice when a word doesn't fit — because in Menzoberranzan, language is law, and law is lethal.
source_quote: The second thing Menzoberranzan trains you for — and this one is equally useful but considerably less comfortable — is to notice when a word doesn't fit.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is known by a diminutive form, Daz'issin, meaning 'small shadow,' likely used by a mother wishing for a child's survival, and is the only known living bearer of the name in the past three centuries.

subject: Yvenne
fact: Yvenne is a keeper of restricted knowledge regarding Menzoberranzan's noble lineages, deliberately withholding information about Daz's origins while maintaining the appearance of neutrality, and has been physically signaling dissonance with her words for five minutes.

subject: Houses that used Daz'issin
fact: The noble houses that historically bore the name Daz'issin have all perished within the past three centuries, with none surviving to the present day.

subject: *Geography and Cities, Menzoberranzan, Pillars of Woe*
fact: A two-hundred-year-old heraldry text, deliberately defaced fifty years ago by a razor cut that removed an appendix referenced by a footnote concerning the name Daz'issin.

subject: defacement of the heraldry text
fact: An appendix referencing Daz'issin was surgically excised from the book with a razor, indicating intentional suppression of lineage records rather than decay or neglect.

subject: Daz's true lineage
fact: The suppression of Daz'issin's record and Yvenne's evasive behavior suggest Daz's origin is tied to a destroyed house whose existence contradicts the official record, and whose survival may still be possible.

subject: Menzoberranzan
fact: Menzoberranzan is a city where reading body language and silences is a survival skill, and where the absence of an answer is treated as a recorded response in the ledger of truth.

subject: defacement timing
fact: The appendix was removed at least fifty years ago, placing the erasure before the last known use of the name Daz'issin in recorded history.

subject: Daz's patron
fact: Yvenne redirected inquiry from Daz's name to his patron, implying the identity of his protector may be more significant — or more dangerous — than his own origin.
